name: proteins_api_get_protein
description: Get comprehensive protein information from Proteins API by UniProt accession. Returns protein annotations, sequences, features, and cross-references. Supports batch operations: pass a list of accessions or comma-separated string to retrieve multiple proteins in parallel.

accession.description: UniProt protein accession(s). Can be a single accession (e.g., 'P05067'), comma-separated string (e.g., 'P05067,P04637'), or list (e.g., ['P05067', 'P04637']). Use UniProt search or ebi_search_domain with domain='uniprot' to find valid accessions.

format.description: Response format. JSON is recommended for most use cases.

oneOf.description: Single protein information (when single accession provided) including annotations, sequences, features, and cross-references. Contains fields: accession, id, proteinExistence, info, organism, secondaryAccession, protein, gene, comments, features, dbReferences, references, etc.

accession.description: Primary UniProtKB accession, e.g. 'P05067'. The stable key for the protein; secondaryAccession lists the ones merged into it.

id.description: UniProtKB entry name, e.g. 'A4_HUMAN'. Readable but NOT stable across releases -- cite the accession.

secondaryAccession.description: Accessions that were merged into this entry, e.g. ['B2R5V1', ...]. An old dataset keyed on one of these still means this protein.

proteinExistence.description: How strongly the protein's existence is supported: 'Evidence at protein level', 'Evidence at transcript level', 'Inferred from homology', 'Predicted', 'Uncertain'. The first line of quality control on any UniProt entry.

type.description: 'Swiss-Prot' for a manually reviewed entry, 'TrEMBL' for an automatically annotated one. This single word decides how much of the rest was checked by a human.

version.description: Entry version number, e.g. 321. Increments on every change; use with `modified` to pin what you read.

names.description: The organism's names, each {type, value} where type is 'scientific' or 'common'.

lineage.description: Taxonomic lineage from the top down, e.g. ['Eukaryota', 'Metazoa', ...].

gene.description: Genes encoding the protein, each with a primary name and synonyms. More than one entry means the protein is encoded by more than one gene.

name.description: The gene's primary symbol, e.g. 'APP', with the evidence for it -- ECO:0000312 means it was taken from HGNC.

evidences.description: What this statement rests on. Each entry is {code, source}: `code` is an ECO term -- ECO:0000269 is experimental evidence from a named publication, ECO:0000250 is inferred by similarity from another protein, ECO:0000305 is a curator's inference, ECO:0000303 is a statement taken from a paper without experiment. An annotation carrying only ECO:0000250 has never been shown in THIS protein.

id.description: That source's identifier, e.g. '10097173' for a PubMed id or 'P12023' for the protein the annotation was projected from.

url.description: Canonical URL for the source record.

alternativeUrl.description: A second URL for the same record, e.g. the Europe PMC copy of a PubMed entry.

synonyms.description: Other symbols for the gene, each with its own evidence. This is what makes an older paper's symbol resolvable.
